summary: Funded by the UK government's Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office, Commonwealth Master's Scholarships pay for a one-year taught master's in the UK for talented candidates from eligible low- and middle-income Commonwealth countries.
covers: Approved return airfare between your home country and the UK.
A monthly stipend of £1,712, or £2,000 at universities in the London area (2027–28 rates).
A study travel grant, and allowances for single, widowed or divorced parents bringing children (£622 a month for the first child).
eligibility: Citizens of — or refugees in — one of the 40+ eligible Commonwealth countries.
A first degree of at least upper second-class (2:1) standard, or a lower second-class degree plus a relevant postgraduate qualification.
A commitment to return home at the end of the award — switching to a Graduate or other UK visa is not permitted.
Nomination by your country's national nominating agency or an approved NGO: the CSC does not accept direct applications.
how_to_apply: Check your national nominating agency's rules and internal deadline — it may be earlier than the CSC's.
Choose up to three eligible UK master's courses.
Complete the CSC online application by 16:00 BST on Tuesday 20 October 2026.
Nominated candidates are notified of the result around July 2027.
watch_out: Your nominating agency may close weeks before 20 October — find its date first.
The return commitment is enforced; the award is for people who plan to work at home.
The CSC never charges fees and never contacts candidates through social-media messages.

sources.title: Commonwealth Scholarship Commission — Commonwealth Master's Scholarships

costs: Covered in full, by agreement between the CSC and your university
Return airfare between home and the UK
Living costs: £1,712 a month, or £2,000 in the London area (2027–28 rates)
An English test such as IELTS
Not required by the CSC — you pay only if your chosen university asks for one
documents: A copy of your valid passport, or proof of refugee status in an eligible Commonwealth country
Full transcripts of all your higher education, with certified translations if not in English
References from at least two people, as signed PDFs on institutional letterhead
Up to three eligible UK master's courses, and statements that address the selection criteria: academic merit, the quality of your proposal and the impact on your home country's development
Your national nominating agency's own forms, submitted by its deadline

faq.a: Not for the scholarship: the CSC does not require any candidate to take an IELTS test. Your UK university may still have its own English requirement.
On three things: your academic merit and experience, the quality of your proposal, and the potential impact of your studies on your home country's development.
The CSC's online application closes at 16:00 BST on Tuesday 20 October 2026 — but your nominating agency usually closes earlier, so find its date first.
